mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% MoM signals a weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS MoM < -1% does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in 3 months signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over 3 months signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the easing signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a strong supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% MoM signals strengthening demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals labor market contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decrease does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% QoQ signals economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if accompanied by a rise in unemployment (UNRATE).
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decrease does not correlate with subsequent negative returns when UNRATE is rising.
